def-qft-qed-physical-gauge-quantities.physical_scope: Charge and gauge-field conversions for the selected flat-space QED model, in the stated SI and natural normalizations; no charge value, running law, regulator, boundary charge sector, or interacting continuum construction is inferred.

def-qft-qed-physical-gauge-quantities:
## Definition

Use the oriented, time-oriented Minkowski model, length coordinates, metric,
and SI/natural dictionary of [[def-qft-framework-units]], with
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $x^0=ct$. Use the gamma matrices,
Dirac adjoint, and effective Clifford metric of
[[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]: $\gamma^0=\beta$, $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$,
and $\bar\psi=\psi^\dagger\beta$. Assume Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]] for the mathematical QFT gauge-data supplier; the
unit conversions below do not themselves spend a choice principle.

Identify the SI charge and mass symbols $q,m$ in
[[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]] with $q_{\rm SI},m_{\rm SI}$ here. Its natural
coupling $g$ is $q_{\rm n}$ below, and its inverse-length mass $\mu$ is the
same $m_{\rm SI}c/\hbar$.

Let $q_{\rm SI}\in\mathbb R$ be a selected charge parameter in coulombs and
$m_{\rm SI}>0$ a selected rest-mass parameter in kilograms. They are inputs
of the chosen model; neither is derived from Maxwell's equations. Set
$\mu=m_{\rm SI}c/\hbar$ in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and
$q_{\rm n}=q_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}$, which is dimensionless under the
framework units of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. For an electron use
$q_{\rm SI}=-e_{\rm SI}$ and
$e_{\rm n}=e_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}>0$, so $q_{\rm n}=-e_{\rm n}$.
Use $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ with the measured current-SI
$\mu_0$ of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. These definitions therefore do not
assign an exact numerical value to $q_{\rm n}$, $e_{\rm n}$, or
$\varepsilon_0$.

In a named inertial chart, let $A^\mu_{\rm SI}=(\varphi/c,\mathbf A)$ be the
electromagnetic potential when one is supplied, with components in
$\mathrm{T\,m}$ under [[def-em-si-conventions]] and
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]. Define the canonical potential and
field-strength components by

$$a^\mu:=\frac{A^\mu_{\rm SI}}{\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}},\qquad f^{\mu\nu}:=\frac{F^{\mu\nu}_{\rm SI}}{\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}}.$$

They have engineering dimensions $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $\mathrm m^{-2}$,
respectively. With the metric-lowered potential
$A_{{\rm SI},a}=\eta_{ab}A^b_{\rm SI}$, the potential component convention is
$A_{{\rm SI},0}=-\varphi/c$ and $A_{{\rm SI},i}=A_i$. The covariant derivative
in the selected QED model is

$$D_a:=\partial_a-iq_{\rm n}a_a =\partial_a-\frac{iq_{\rm SI}}{\hbar}A_{{\rm SI},a},$$

since $q_{\rm n}a_a=q_{\rm SI}A_{{\rm SI},a}/\hbar$. Both terms in $D_a$
have unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$. If the SI gauge function $\chi$ has unit
$\mathrm{Wb}=\mathrm{T\,m^2}$, then $q_{\rm SI}\chi/\hbar$ is dimensionless;
the corresponding natural gauge function
$\lambda=\chi/\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}$ is dimensionless and
$q_{\rm n}\lambda=q_{\rm SI}\chi/\hbar$. These conversions apply to smooth
local gauge transformations; they assert no boundary condition, asymptotic
charge sector, or global gauge-fixing result.

If a separately specified finite regulator introduces Hamiltonian
eigenvalues, they have unit joule; this definition introduces no regulator.
The field components and units refer to the selected inertial chart, not to a
new observer congruence or a cross-framework identification.

post-qft-free-photon-model.physical_scope: The selected source-free, flat Minkowski Maxwell photon model with a positive transverse one-particle Hilbert space, its constructed bosonic Fock representation and free dynamics, and actual smeared field-strength and bounded Weyl observables; no interacting continuum QED or empirical outcome is asserted.

post-qft-free-photon-model:
## Postulate

Adopt the following specified free-photon model in the oriented,
time-oriented affine Minkowski spacetime and length coordinates of
[[def-qft-framework-units]], with metric $(-,+,+,+)$ and $x^0=ct$. The
classical electromagnetic input is the smooth source-free branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the electromagnetic two-form and its potential
components are those of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and a supplied
potential is subject to [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. These EM suppliers
are physical input and conventions: they do not by themselves construct a
quantum representation.

For almost every $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, set
$\mathbf n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and
$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^{\mathsf T}$. The mathematical
definition [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]] specifies the positive
one-photon Hilbert space

$$\mathcal H_T= \{u\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3): \mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ for almost every }\mathbf k\},$$

with the inherited pairing
$\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int\overline{u(\mathbf k)}\cdot v(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k$,
linear in the second variable as in [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. The
value assigned to $P_T$ at
$\mathbf k=0$ is immaterial because that point has Lebesgue measure zero; no
continuous polarization frame over all momentum directions is chosen. Adopt
the bosonic Fock representation $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$ and the free
Hamiltonian

$$H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|),$$

where on the $n$-photon sector $d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|)$ is multiplication by
$\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|$ and is zero on the vacuum sector. Its exact
self-adjoint domain and the unitary mass-cone action are those in the
mathematical supplier [[lem-qft-photon-covariance-spectrum]]. The actual
smeared field-strength distributions and bounded Weyl operators are those
constructed in [[lem-qft-photon-local-weyl-observables]]; a pointwise
potential or field-strength operator is not asserted to exist. These
mathematical suppliers are draft carriers with mixed current Step 1 status: the
transverse-space, null-quotient, covariance-spectrum, framework-units, and
C01 measurement carriers have current ready records; the local-Weyl carrier is
escalated through its field-strength prerequisite. Readiness records are not
independent approval, and every use remains conditional on the exact statement
and proof supplied.

For the physical interpretation of an actually constructed state and a
supplied normalized measurement instrument, use
[[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]]: Born probabilities are
assigned only to that specified model and instrument. This postulate records
the model's free Maxwell quanta as photons. It does not assert that the
model has been empirically confirmed, and it introduces no interacting
four-dimensional QED Hilbert space, scattering operator, LSZ limit,
asymptotic completeness, or nonperturbative continuum limit. In calculations
using an indefinite four-polarization auxiliary space, only the positive
transverse model or its separately constructed null quotient is physical;
four auxiliary components are not four positive photon states.

post-qft-qed-local-coupling.physical_scope: A smooth local classical Maxwell–Dirac coupling in the stated SI/natural conventions, with electron charge q=-e as the selected QED species and the separately adopted free photon and Dirac representations; it asserts no interacting continuum Hilbert space, global PDE solution, pointwise quantum current, scattering operator, or nonperturbative QED construction.

post-qft-qed-local-coupling:
## Postulate

Adopt a smooth local classical Maxwell–Dirac model on an open region of the
flat spacetime specified by [[def-qft-framework-units]]. Let $A_{{\rm SI},a}$
be a supplied real $C^\infty$ electromagnetic covector potential and let
$\psi:\!U\to\mathbb C^4$ be a $C^\infty$ commuting spinor field. The charge
$q_{\rm SI}$ and rest mass $m_{\rm SI}>0$ are model inputs; for the electron
take $q_{\rm SI}=-e_{\rm SI}$. Use the component, metric, Clifford, charge,
field-normalization, and unit conventions of
[[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]], [[def-qft-qed-physical-gauge-quantities]],
[[def-qft-framework-units]], and the electromagnetic suppliers of
[[post-qft-free-photon-model]]. In particular,
$D_a=\partial_a-iq_{\rm SI}A_{{\rm SI},a}/\hbar
=\partial_a-iq_{\rm n}a_a$ and $\mu=m_{\rm SI}c/\hbar$.

Adopt the local action density in natural normalization

$$\mathcal L_{\rm nat} =-\frac14 f_{ab}f^{ab} +\frac{i}{2}\bigl(\bar\psi\gamma^aD_a\psi -(D_a\bar\psi)\gamma^a\psi\bigr)-\mu\bar\psi\psi,$$

where $f_{ab}=\partial_a a_b-\partial_ba_a$ on the region where the
potential is supplied, $\bar\psi=\psi^\dagger\beta$, and
$D_a\bar\psi=\partial_a\bar\psi+iq_{\rm n}a_a\bar\psi$. The physical action
is $S_{\rm cl}=\hbar\int_U\mathcal L_{\rm nat}\,d^4x$ with $x^0=ct$. For
compactly supported local variations this is the adopted classical
Maxwell–Dirac formulation; its Euler–Lagrange consequences are not postulated
as a proof in this item.

For a smooth gauge function $\chi$ in webers, the adopted local
transformation is
$A_{{\rm SI},a}\mapsto A_{{\rm SI},a}+\partial_a\chi$ and
$\psi\mapsto e^{iq_{\rm SI}\chi/\hbar}\psi$. It leaves $F=dA$ invariant and
makes $D_a\psi$ transform by the same phase. This is the covector form of the
SI potential rule in [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. Gauge functions in the
local variation argument are compactly supported; no assertion is made about
large gauge transformations, nontrivial bundles, boundary charges, or
asymptotic sectors.

The model adopts the separately specified free Dirac representation of
[[post-qft-free-field-model]] and the positive free photon representation of
[[post-qft-free-photon-model]] as the free-field correspondence used to
describe the selected species. This extra correspondence does not quantize
the interacting classical action. In particular, this postulate supplies no
interacting continuum four-dimensional QED Hilbert space, no globally
well-posed coupled PDE, no pointwise operator-valued composite current, no
scattering or LSZ construction, and no regulator-removal or
nonperturbative-existence result.

pthm-qft-photon-physical-properties.physical_scope: The selected flat-space source-free photon model only: positive transverse one-photon states, the auxiliary null quotient, Lorentz-covariant free dynamics, and its exact Hamiltonian domain; no interacting gauge model or empirical photon state is asserted.

pthm-qft-photon-physical-properties:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] for the selected Fock-space
construction, with the positive constants and physical energy units of
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. In the adopted model [[post-qft-free-photon-model]], for
$\mathbf k\ne0$ set $\mathbf n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and
$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^{\mathsf T}$. Then for almost every
nonzero momentum, $P_T(\mathbf k)$ is a positive orthogonal projection of
rank two, and the positive one-photon Hilbert space is its closed range
$\mathcal H_T\subset L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)$. This
description chooses no global continuous polarization frame.

If an auxiliary four-polarization space
$\mathcal K=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^4)$ with indefinite form
$[\epsilon,\delta]=\int\epsilon^\dagger\eta\delta\,d^3\mathbf k$ is used,
the physical subsidiary space
$\mathcal K_0=\{\epsilon:-\epsilon^0+\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\epsilon=0
\text{ a.e.}\}$ has null radical
$\mathcal N=\{b(\mathbf k)(1,\mathbf n):b\in L^2\}$. The quotient
$\mathcal K_0/\mathcal N$ is isometric to $\mathcal H_T$ with positive
inner product. The physical Fock Hamiltonian
$H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|)$ is self-adjoint, nonnegative, and
has the exact domain and strongly continuous Lorentz-covariant mass-cone
action in [[lem-qft-photon-covariance-spectrum]]. The vector-valued
auxiliary space is not a positive state space, and none of its negative
directions is assigned a negative Born probability.

pthm-qft-photon-local-observables.physical_scope: Gauge-invariant observables of the specified positive transverse free-photon Fock model, smeared with compactly supported real tests; local commutativity applies to spacelike-separated supports, while the Coulomb-gauge potential is not claimed local.

pthm-qft-photon-local-observables:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] for the constructed Fock
representation. In the adopted model [[post-qft-free-photon-model]], let
$h^{ab}\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{1,3};\mathbb R)$ be a real antisymmetric
two-tensor test. Here $f_{ab}$ is the natural-normalized field-strength
distribution of the selected free model, corresponding to $F_{ab}$ in the
mathematical free-photon suppliers and distinct from the SI tensor
$F_{{\rm SI},ab}$. Its smearing
$$f(h)=\frac12\int f_{ab}(x)h^{ab}(x)\,d^4x$$
is a well-defined operator-valued distribution on the common finite-particle
domain $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$, not a pointwise field operator. It is gauge
invariant and covariant under the selected free mass-cone unitary action.
For two such tests with spacelike-separated supports,
$[f(h),f(\ell)]=0$ on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. Let $g_h$ be the associated
one-particle test vector and define the Weyl observable
$W_h:=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2\,g_h)$ as in
[[lem-qft-photon-local-weyl-observables]]. These are bounded unitaries of
norm one; their real and imaginary parts are bounded Hermitian operators
and commute for spacelike-separated supports. No locality claim is made for
a Coulomb-gauge potential.

pthm-qft-qed-classical-coupling.physical_scope: The smooth local classical Maxwell–Dirac branch on an open flat Minkowski domain, with compactly supported variations and the stated SI signs; it does not assert a global coupled PDE solution, an interacting quantum representation, or a pointwise quantum current.

pthm-qft-qed-classical-coupling:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] for the selected free-field
correspondence in [[post-qft-qed-local-coupling]]. Let $U$ be an open subset
of flat Minkowski spacetime with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and
length coordinates $x^0=ct$. Let $A_{{\rm SI},a}:U\to\mathbb R$ be a supplied
$C^\infty$ covector potential, let
$\psi:U\to\mathbb C^4$ be a $C^\infty$ commuting spinor, and take a selected
real charge $q_{\rm SI}$ and mass $m_{\rm SI}>0$ with the conventions of
[[def-qft-qed-physical-gauge-quantities]] and
[[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. Use independent compactly supported smooth
variations of $A_{\rm SI}$ and of both real and imaginary components of $\psi$. If $(A_{\rm SI},\psi)$ is stationary
for the adopted classical action, then

$$\bigl(i\gamma^aD_a-\mu\bigr)\psi=0,\qquad \partial_aF_{\rm SI}^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad \partial_aj^a=0,$$

where $D_a=\partial_a-iq_{\rm SI}A_{{\rm SI},a}/\hbar$,
$\mu=m_{\rm SI}c/\hbar$, and
$j^a=q_{\rm SI}c\,\bar\psi\gamma^a\psi$. In laboratory components this
current is $\rho_q=q_{\rm SI}\psi^\dagger\psi$ and
$\mathbf J_q=q_{\rm SI}c\,\psi^\dagger\boldsymbol\alpha\psi$, so
$j=(c\rho_q,\mathbf J_q)$. Together with $F=dA$ on the supplied potential
domain, the field equation and Bianchi identity have exactly the smooth SI
Maxwell signs in [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. The current and spinor here are
classical smooth commuting fields; this statement is not a construction of a
pointwise quantum composite operator.

pthm-qft-qed-coulomb-constraints.physical_scope: The explicit smooth, periodic, neutral Gauss branch on a flat three-torus, with a zero-mean Coulomb potential, plus the separate finite-mode classical commuting-spinor primary-constraint calculation; no nonneutral periodic solution, continuum quantum density product, or CAR derivation is asserted.

pthm-qft-qed-coulomb-constraints:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] for the torus Fourier
construction. Let $L>0$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time
interval, and let the spatial domain be the flat torus
$\mathbb T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, where $L$ is a positive length
in metres. Coordinates use $x^0=ct$ with $t$ in seconds under
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. Use the smooth classical branch of
[[post-qft-qed-local-coupling]] with smooth periodic electromagnetic
potentials and spinor. Here $\psi$ has the canonical length dimension
$\mathrm m^{-3/2}$ of [[def-qft-framework-units]], so the scalar-potential
source $\rho_q:=q_{\rm SI}\psi^\dagger\psi$ has unit $\mathrm{C,m^{-3}}$.
On stationary solutions it agrees
with the current density in [[pthm-qft-qed-classical-coupling]]. Use the
gamma-matrix and
$\alpha,\beta$ conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. In Coulomb gauge
$\operatorname{div}\mathbf A=0$, the multiplier equation for any smooth
periodic configuration is
$\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol\pi_A+\rho_q=0$. On the explicitly neutral
branch
$\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}\rho_q(\mathbf x,t)\,d^3\mathbf x=0$ for every $t\in I$,
the zero-mean scalar potential is the unique smooth periodic solution of
$-\Delta\varphi=\rho_q/\varepsilon_0$. With
$\widehat\rho_q(\mathbf n,t)=L^{-3}\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}
\rho_q(\mathbf x,t)e^{-2\pi i\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf x/L}\,d^3\mathbf x$ and
$\boldsymbol\kappa_{\mathbf n}=2\pi\mathbf n/L$, the longitudinal energy is

$$\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}|\nabla\varphi|^2\,d^3\mathbf x =\frac12\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}\rho_q\varphi\,d^3\mathbf x =\frac{L^3}{2\varepsilon_0} \sum_{\mathbf n\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}} \frac{|\widehat\rho_q(\mathbf n,t)|^2}{|\boldsymbol\kappa_{\mathbf n}|^2} \ge0.$$

The corresponding classical Hamiltonian, before imposing the Gauss
constraint, contains

$$H=\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}\left[ \frac{|\boldsymbol\pi_A|^2}{2\varepsilon_0} +\frac{|\mathbf B|^2}{2\mu_0} +\psi^\dagger\!\left(c\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot (-i\hbar\nabla-q_{\rm SI}\mathbf A)+\beta m_{\rm SI}c^2\right)\!\psi +\varphi(\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol\pi_A+\rho_q) \right]d^3\mathbf x,$$

with $\pi_\varphi=0$ the primary multiplier momentum. In a separate
truncation to $N\ge1$ orthonormal spatial spinor modes, let $z_j,\bar z_j$
be dimensionless commuting complex-coordinate notation with canonical
brackets $\{z_j,p_k\}=\delta_{jk}$,
$\{\bar z_j,\bar p_k\}=\delta_{jk}$ and all other elementary brackets zero.
For $\hbar>0$, the symmetrized first-order Dirac kinetic term gives the
primary constraints
$C_j=p_j-i\hbar\bar z_j/2$ and
$\bar C_j=\bar p_j+i\hbar z_j/2$ with invertible mixed bracket matrix
$-i\hbar I_N$. This finite-dimensional classical calculation does not
derive fermionic CAR. The neutral torus branch is an explicit hypothesis.
For the selected electron, $q_{\rm SI}=-e_{\rm SI}\ne0$, so a neutral
single-species commuting-spinor configuration has $\psi=0$; no nontrivial
neutral charged classical Dirac configuration is asserted. The finite-mode
constraint calculation is separate and does not claim to be a solution in
that branch.

texp-qft-photon-auxiliary-comparison.physical_scope: A hypothetical exact comparison between an indefinite auxiliary four-polarization vector and normalized states in the positive transverse free-photon model; no measurement, negative probability, or empirical event is asserted.

texp-qft-photon-auxiliary-comparison:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] and the positive transverse
free-photon model of [[pthm-qft-photon-physical-properties]]. Let
$\mathcal K=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^4)$ carry the indefinite
form $[\epsilon,\delta]=\int\epsilon^\dagger
\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)\delta\,d^3\mathbf k$. For nonzero
$\mathbf k$, put $\mathbf n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and define the subsidiary
subspace by
$\mathcal K_0=\{\epsilon:-\epsilon^0+\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\epsilon=0
\text{ almost everywhere}\}$. Fix a wave-number scale $\kappa>0$ in
$\mathrm m^{-1}$ under [[def-qft-framework-units]], and let $\Omega$ be the
momentum ball of radius $\kappa/4$ centered at $\kappa(0,0,1)$. By
[[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]], translate a smooth
bump $b$ that equals one on the concentric ball of radius $\kappa/8$ and
has support in $\Omega$. Set $g=b/\|b\|_2$, so
$g\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and $\|g\|_2=1$. The auxiliary timelike wavepacket
$\epsilon_{\rm aux}(\mathbf k)=g(\mathbf k)(1,0,0,0)$ has
$[\epsilon_{\rm aux},\epsilon_{\rm aux}]=-1$ but is not in $\mathcal K_0$.
By contrast, a normalized transverse wavepacket in
$\mathcal H_T$ represents a positive physical one-photon state. Therefore
the negative auxiliary norm is not a negative Born probability.

texp-qft-qed-neutral-cell.physical_scope: A hypothetical smooth periodic Gauss-law branch on a flat three-torus with no boundary, puncture, or charge-compensating exterior; nonzero total charge is inconsistent with the stated periodic constraint. No real apparatus or observed charged cell is asserted.

texp-qft-qed-neutral-cell:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] and the smooth Maxwell
branch of [[post-qft-qed-local-coupling]]. On
$\mathbb T_L^3$ with side length $L>0$ in metres, choose the electron charge
$q_{\rm SI}=-e_{\rm SI}<0$ and a constant nonzero smooth commuting spinor
$\psi(\mathbf x)=\psi_0\in\mathbb C^4$ in the canonical length normalization
of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. Its source
$\rho_q=q_{\rm SI}\psi_0^\dagger\psi_0$ is smooth and periodic, with SI
charge-density unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$ under the stated field normalization,
and its total charge is
$Q=q_{\rm SI}\psi_0^\dagger\psi_0L^3\ne0$. In a hypothetical periodic
configuration with no boundary, puncture, or exterior compensating flux,
no smooth periodic electric momentum can satisfy the adopted Gauss
constraint
$\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol\pi_A+\rho_q=0$. The neutral case
$Q=0$ is the separate branch supplied by
[[pthm-qft-qed-coulomb-constraints]] and
[[lem-qft-qed-coulomb-constraint]]. The setup is a thought experiment,
not a report of a physical measurement. The constant spinor is a
hypothetical field configuration; no Dirac stationarity or observed
charged cell is asserted.
